# Anthropic Committed to Spend $900 Billion. Wall Street Expects Its Debt to Be Junk.

## After a turbulent IPO, the company’s credit rating will affect its capital plans and the future of the AI industry

By 

Matt Wirz

 and 

Jack Pitcher

Updated Nov. 23, 2026 9:20 am ET

Play video![Anthropic Shares Close Up After Historic IPO](https://images.wsj.net/im-05309039?width=860&size=1.7778)

Keep hovering to play

Anthropic made history with its initial price offering, raising $81 billion. WSJ’s Kate Clark breaks down the artificial-intelligence giant’s first day of trading. Photo: Shuran Huang for WSJ

Anthropic’s ANT 0.25% increase; green up pointing triangle stock market debut was rocky. There are even bigger questions about how it will fare in the bond market.

The hot artificial-intelligence company raised more than $100 billion last week and is worth around $1.18 trillion, above Walmart or JPMorgan Chase. But it has committed to spend some $900 billion in the coming years to pay for the gargantuan amount of computing power needed for its leading AI models.
